title: Solid-state stack pressure management
bottleneck: Solid-state cells need carefully controlled stack pressure — high enough to maintain interfacial contact and suppress lithium voiding, low enough to avoid lithium creep into the electrolyte and mechanical fracture. The 2026 eScience review shows pressure is a double-edged sword: it fixes voiding during cycling but drives creep damage during storage. No cell design yet self-regulates pressure across temperature and state-of-charge swings.
why_it_blocks: External pressure frames add mass, volume, and cost that directly erode the energy-density advantage solid-state batteries promise. If every pack needs a precision pressure vessel, the technology may never beat advanced liquid cells on system-level metrics.
current_state: Compliant interlayers and pressure-tolerant cell architectures are under development, and some pilot designs accept modest external pressure. But a truly pressure-agnostic solid-state cell — one that survives the pressure swings of real automotive service — does not exist.
